translations.text: Since many have wanted to write accounts of the events that we firmly believe,
just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word,
it seemed right to me too, since I have carefully followed everything, to write it all for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you may know the truth of the things you have been taught.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, from the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was a descendant of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
Both of them were righteous before God, living blamelessly according to all the Lord’s commandments and righteous requirements.
But they had no child, because Elizabeth was unable to conceive, and both of them were advanced in years.
Now while he was serving as priest before God, when his division was on duty,
according to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him to offer incense, and he entered the Lord’s temple.
The whole crowd of people was praying outside at the time of the incense offering.
An angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing to the right of the incense altar.
Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear came over him.
The angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John.
You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before the Lord. He will drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit while still in his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the people of Israel back to the Lord their God.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah the prophet, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children, and the disobedient to the understanding of the righteous, and to make ready for the Lord a people made complete.”
Zechariah said to the angel, “How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years.”
The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands before God. I was sent to speak with you and bring you this good news.
From now on you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe these words of mine, which will be fulfilled at their appointed time.”
Meanwhile, the people stood waiting for Zechariah and were wondering at his delay in the temple.
When Zechariah came out, he could not speak to them. They realized that he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making gestures to them and remained unable to speak.
When his days of service were completed, he went home.
After those days, his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself secluded for five months. She said,
“This is what the Lord has done for me in the days when he looked upon me, to take away my disgrace among people.”
In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to Galilee, to a town named Nazareth,
to a virgin engaged to a man named Joseph, from the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.
The angel came to her and said, “Peace to you, full of grace! Our Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.”
But when she saw him, she was troubled by his words and wondered what this greeting meant.
The angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
For look, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.
He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and his kingdom will have no end.”
Mary said to the angel, “How will this happen, since I have not had sexual relations with a man?”
The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore, the one to be born in you is holy and will be called the Son of God.
And look, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age. This is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
For nothing is too difficult for God.”
Mary said, “Here I am, the Lord’s servant. Let it happen to me according to your word.” Then the angel left her.
In those days Mary got up and hurried to the hill country, to a town of Judah.
She entered Zechariah’s house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She cried out in a loud voice and said to Mary, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
How has this come to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For look, when the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby leaped in my womb with great joy.
Blessed is she who believed that the things spoken to her by the Lord would be fulfilled.”
Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior,
because he has looked upon the lowly condition of his servant. For look, from now on all generations will call me blessed,
because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and his name is holy.
His mercy is upon those who fear him, through the ages and generations.
He has won victory with his arm and scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
He has brought down the powerful from their thrones and lifted up the humble.
He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty-handed.
He has helped Israel his servant and remembered his mercy,
as he spoke to our ancestors, to Abraham and his descendants forever.
Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months and then returned to her home.
Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that God had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling him Zechariah after his father.
But his mother answered them, “No! He is to be called John.”
They said to her, “There is no one in your family called by this name.”
They made signs to his father to find out what he wanted to name him.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” Everyone was amazed.
Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he spoke and blessed God.
Fear came over all their neighbors, and all these things were talked about throughout the hill country of Judea.
All who heard pondered these things in their hearts, saying, “What, then, will this child become?” And the Lord’s hand was with him.
His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
“Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited his people and brought them deliverance.
He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David,
as he spoke through the mouths of his holy prophets from long ago,
to save us from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us.
He has shown mercy to our ancestors and remembered his holy covenants
and the oaths he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that we might be rescued from the hand of our enemies and serve before him without fear,
all our days, in uprightness and righteousness.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his way,
to give his people knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins,
through the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
to shine on those who sit in darkness and in the shadows of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He lived in the wilderness until the day when he was revealed to Israel.
In those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the people of his dominion should be registered.
This was the first registration, during the governorship of Quirinius in Syria.
Everyone went to be registered in their own town.
Joseph also went up from Nazareth, a town in Galilee, to Judea, to David’s town, which is called Bethlehem, because he belonged to the house and family of David,
with Mary, his betrothed, who was pregnant, so that he could be registered there.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in strips of cloth, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them where they were lodging.
There were shepherds in that region, camping there and keeping watch over their flocks at night.
And look, an angel of God came to them, and the glory of the Lord shone upon them, and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, “Do not be afraid, for look, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for the whole world.
For today a Savior has been born for you in David’s town, who is the Lord, the Messiah.
This will be the sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a manger.”
Suddenly many heavenly armies appeared with the angel, praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest heavens, and on earth peace and good hope for humanity!”
When the angels had gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds spoke to one another, saying, “Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, as the Lord has made known to us.”
They came in a hurry and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger.
When they saw him, they made known what had been told them about the child.
Everyone who heard was amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these words and pondered them in her heart.
Those shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for everything they had seen and heard, just as they had been told.
When eight days had passed and it was time for the child to be circumcised, he was named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
When the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord.
As it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.”
And they were to offer a sacrifice, as prescribed in the law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. This man was upright and righteous, and he was waiting for the consolation of Israel. The Holy Spirit was upon him.
The Holy Spirit had told him that he would not see death until he had seen the Lord’s Messiah.
He came to the temple in the Spirit. When his parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him what was commanded in the law,
he took him into his arms, blessed God, and said:
“Now, my Lord, you are releasing your servant in peace, according to your word,
for my eyes have seen your mercy,
which you have prepared in the sight of all nations:
a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and glory for your people Israel.”
Joseph and his mother were amazed at the things being said about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, “Look, this child is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and as a sign of contention.
A spear will pierce your own soul too, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
There was also Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She too was very old. She had lived with her husband for seven years after marrying as a virgin.
She had been a widow for about eighty-four years. She never left the temple, but served with fasting and prayer, day and night.
She too stood up at that very hour and gave thanks to the Lord. She spoke about him with everyone who was waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
When they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong in spirit and was filled with wisdom. God’s grace was upon him.
His family went to Jerusalem every year for the Passover festival.
When he was twelve years old, they went up to the festival as they customarily did.
When the days were over, they started back, but the child Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother did not know.
For they thought he was with their traveling companions. After they had traveled a day’s journey, they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
They did not find him, so they returned again to Jerusalem, searching for him.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard him was amazed at his wisdom and his answers.
When they saw him, they were amazed. His mother said to him, “My son, why have you done this to us? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great distress.”
He said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
But they did not understand what he said to them.
He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
Jesus grew in stature and wisdom, and in favor with God and people.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip was tetrarch of Iturea and the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
He went throughout the whole region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, who said, “The voice of one calling in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, and make straight paths on the plain for our God.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ground will become a plain.
And all humanity will see the salvation of God.’”
He would say to the crowds who came to him to be baptized, “You offspring of vipers! Who showed you how to flee from the coming wrath?
So produce fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.”
But look, the axe is laid at the root of the trees. So every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and falls into the fire.
The crowds asked him, “What, then, should we do?”
He answered them, “Anyone who has two tunics should give to someone who has none, and anyone who has food should do the same.”
Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He said to them, “Do not demand anything more than you have been instructed to collect.”
Soldiers also asked him, “What should we do?” He said to them, “Do not use violence against anyone or oppress anyone, and be content with your pay.”
The people were full of expectation about John, and all of them were wondering in their hearts whether he might be the Messiah.
John answered them, “I baptize you with water, but someone more powerful than I is coming. I am not worthy to untie the straps of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
He holds a winnowing shovel in his hand and clears his threshing floors. He gathers the wheat into his storehouses, but he will burn the chaff with fire that cannot be put out.”
He also taught many other things and proclaimed the good news to the people.
But Herod the tetrarch, because John rebuked him over Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, and over all the evil things he was doing,
added this to them all: he locked John up in prison.
When all the people had been baptized, Jesus was also baptized. As he was praying, heaven opened,
and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in the bodily form of a dove. A voice came from heaven, saying, “You are my beloved Son; I am pleased with you.”
Now Jesus himself was about thirty years old and was thought to be the son of Joseph, the son of Heli.
The son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph.
The son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai.
The son of Maath, the son of Matthat, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah.
The son of John, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri.
Son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmodad, son of Er.
Son of Jose, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, son of Levi.
The son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliaki[?].
The son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David.
The son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon.
The son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah.
The son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor.
The son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah.
The son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech.
The son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan.
The son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, who was from God.
Now Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and the Spirit led him into the wilderness,
for forty days, to be tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when he had completed them, he was hungry at last.
The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”
Jesus answered him, “It is written: ‘A person does not live on bread alone, but on every word of God.’”
Satan took him up a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the earth in a moment.
The devil said to him, “I will give you all this authority and its glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
So if you bow down before me, it will all be yours.”
Jesus answered him, “It is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone.’”
He brought him to Jerusalem, set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
For it is written: ‘He will command his angels concerning you, to protect you,’
and, ‘They will lift you up in their arms, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.’”
But Jesus answered him, “It is said: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
When the devil had finished all his temptations, he left him for a time.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread throughout the surrounding region.
He taught in their synagogues and was praised by everyone.
He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. As was his custom, he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read.
He was given the scroll of Isaiah the prophet. Jesus opened the scroll and found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. For this reason he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, and to strengthen the broken with forgiveness,
and to proclaim a year acceptable to the Lord.”
He rolled up the scroll, gave it to the attendant, and went and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
He began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
Everyone spoke well of him and marveled at the gracious words coming from his mouth. They said, “Isn't this Joseph's son?”
Jesus said to them, “Perhaps you will say this proverb to me: ‘Doctor, heal yourself!’ And, ‘Do here in your hometown everything we have heard you did in Capernaum.’”
But he said, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
For I tell you the truth: there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah the prophet, when the heavens were shut for three years and six months, and a great famine came over the whole land.
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to a widow in Zarephath in Sidon.
And there were many lepers among the people of Israel in the days of Elisha the prophet, yet none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Aramean.”
When those in the synagogue heard these things, they were all filled with rage.
They got up, drove him out of the town, and brought him to the brow of the hill on which their town was built, intending to throw him off the cliff.
But he passed through their midst and went away.
He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and taught them on the Sabbaths.
They were astonished at his teaching, because his word had authority.
In the synagogue there was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon in him, and he shouted in a loud voice.
And he said, “Leave me alone! What do we have to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him and said, “Be silent and come out of him!” The demon threw the man down in their midst and came out of him without harming him at all.
Great amazement seized everyone, and they spoke to one another, saying, “What is this word that commands unclean spirits with authority and power, and they come out?”
News about him spread throughout the surrounding region.
When Jesus left the synagogue, he entered Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they appealed to him on her behalf.
He stood over her and rebuked her fever, and it left her. Immediately she got up and began serving them.
As the sun was setting, all those who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him. He laid his hand on each one of them and healed them.
Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Messiah, the Son of God!” But he rebuked them and would not let them speak, because they knew that he was the Messiah.
At daybreak he went out to a deserted place. The crowds searched for him and came to where he was, and they held him back so that he would not leave them.
But Jesus said to them, “I must also proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns, because this is why I was sent.”
And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.
Now, as the crowd gathered around him to hear the word of God, he was standing beside the Lake of Gennesaret.
He saw two boats standing at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had gotten out of them and were washing their nets.
One of them belonged to Simon Peter. Jesus got into it and sat down. He asked them to take it a little way from the shore into the water. Then he sat and taught the crowd from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Go out into deep water and let down your net for a catch.”
Simon answered him, “Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But at your word I will let down the net.”
When they did this, they caught a very large number of fish, and their net began to tear.
They signaled to their companions in the other boat to come and help them. When they came, they filled both boats so full that they were close to sinking.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ feet and said to him, “I beg you, Lord, go away from me, because I am a sinful man.”
For amazement had gripped him and everyone with him because of the catch of fish they had taken.
The same was true of James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners. Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid. From now on you will be catching people for life.”
They brought the boats to shore, left everything, and followed him.
While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man covered all over with leprosy came. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him, “I am willing. Be clean!” Immediately his leprosy left him, and he was made clean.
He instructed him, “Do not tell anyone. Instead, go and show yourself to the priests, and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
But the news about him spread all the more, and large crowds gathered to hear him and to be healed of their diseases.
But he would withdraw into the wilderness and pray.

One day, while Jesus was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
Some men brought a paralyzed man on a bed. They were trying to bring him in and place him before him.
When they could not find a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up onto the roof and lowered him with his bed through the roofing into the middle, in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Man, your sins are forgiven.”
The scribes and Pharisees began thinking and saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
But Jesus knew their thoughts and answered them, “What are you thinking in your hearts?
Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—“I tell you, get up, pick up your bed, and go home.”
Immediately he stood up before their eyes, picked up his bed, and went home, praising God.
Amazement seized everyone, and they praised God. They were filled with fear and said, “We have seen wonders today!”
After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office. He said to him, “Follow me.”
He left everything, got up, and followed him.
Levi gave a great banquet for him at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors and others were reclining at the meal with them.
The scribes and Pharisees grumbled and said to his disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy do not need a doctor, but those who are very sick do.”
“I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
But they said to him, “Why do John's disciples fast regularly and pray, as do those of the Pharisees, while yours eat and drink?”
He said to them, “You cannot make the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them.”
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.
He also told them a parable: “No one tears a patch from a new garment and puts it on an old garment. Otherwise, he tears the new garment, and the patch from the new one does not match the old.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine bursts the wineskins, the wine spills out, and the wineskins are ruined.
Instead, new wine is put into new wineskins, and both are preserved.
And no one who drinks old wine immediately wants new wine, for he says, ‘The old is pleasant.’”
On a Sabbath, as Jesus was walking through the grainfields, his disciples were picking heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating.
But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why are you doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?”
Jesus answered them, “Have you not even read what David did when he and those with him were hungry:
how he entered the house of God, took and ate the bread from the Lord's table, and gave it to those with him—bread that only the priests were permitted to eat?”
And he said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
On another Sabbath, he entered the synagogue and was teaching. There was a man there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees were watching him to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they could find grounds to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts and said to the man whose hand was withered, “Get up and come into the middle of the congregation.” And when he came and stood there,
Jesus said to them, “I ask you: What is lawful on the Sabbath—to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?”
He looked around at all of them and said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored, like the other one.
But they were filled with envy and were discussing with one another what they should do to Jesus.
In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and there he spent the night in prayer to God.
When day dawned, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he named apostles.
Simon, whom he named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was called the Zealot;
Judas son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who became a betrayer.

Jesus came down with them and stood on a plain, along with a large crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon,
who had come to hear his message and to be healed of their diseases. Those who were tormented by unclean spirits were also being healed.
The whole crowd was trying to touch him, because power was going out from him and healing them all.
He raised his eyes toward his disciples and said, “Blessed are you who are poor, because the kingdom of God is yours.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, because you will be satisfied. Blessed are you who weep now, because you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, exclude you, insult you, and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and leap for joy, because your reward is great in heaven. For their ancestors treated the prophets in the same way.
But woe to you who are rich, because you have received your comfort.
Woe to you who are full, because you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, because you will weep and mourn.
Woe to you when people speak well of you, because that is how their ancestors treated the false prophets.
But I say to you who are listening: Love your enemies, and do good to those who hate you.
Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
If someone strikes you on your cheek, offer him the other one. If someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic either.
Give to everyone who asks you, and do not demand your belongings back from someone who takes them.
Treat other people just as you want them to treat you.
For if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
And if you lend to someone from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners so that they may be repaid in kind.

But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend without cutting off anyone’s hope. Then your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High, for he is kind to the wicked and the ungrateful.
So be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down and overflowing, will be poured into your laps. For the measure you use will be used to measure out to you.
He also told them a parable: “Can a blind person lead a blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?
No student is greater than his teacher, for everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

Or how can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you do not notice the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly enough to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.
There is no good tree that produces bad fruit, nor a bad tree that produces good fruit.
For every tree is known by its fruit. People do not gather figs from thornbushes, nor do they pick grapes from a bramble.

A good person brings good things out of the good treasures in his heart, and an evil person brings evil things out of the evil treasures in his heart. For the lips speak from what overflows from the heart.
Why do you call me ‘My Lord, my Lord,’ but do not do what I say?
Everyone who comes to me, hears my words, and does them—I will show you what he is like.
He is like a man building a house who dug deep and laid the foundations on rock. When a flood came, it battered that house but could not shake it, because its foundation had been laid on rock.

But the person who hears and does not act is like a man who built his house on the soil without a foundation. When the river battered it, it immediately fell, and the collapse of that house was great.”
When he had finished speaking all these words in the hearing of the people, Jesus entered Capernaum.
Now a certain centurion’s servant, whom he valued highly, was seriously ill and close to death.
He heard about Jesus and sent Jewish elders to him, asking him to come and save his servant’s life.
When they came to Jesus, they pleaded earnestly with him, saying, “He deserves to have you do this for him.”
For he loves our people, and he himself built the synagogue for us.

Jesus went with them. When he was not far from the house, the centurion sent his friends to him with this message: “My Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.
For that reason, I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I too am a man under authority, and I have soldiers under my command. I say to one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.
When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him. He turned and said to the crowd following him, ‘I tell you, not even in Israel have I found faith like this.’
Those who had been sent returned to the house and found the slave who had been sick in good health.
The next day he went to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd went with him.
As he approached the city gate, he saw a dead man being carried out for burial. He was his mother’s only son, and his mother was a widow. A large crowd of people from the city was with her.
When Jesus saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, ‘Do not weep.’
He went over and touched the bier, and those carrying it stood still. He said, ‘Young man, I say to you, get up.’
The dead man sat up and began to speak, and he gave him back to his mother.
Fear seized them all, and they praised God, saying, ‘A great prophet has arisen among us,’ and ‘God has visited his people.’
This report about him spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.
John’s disciples told him about all these things.
John called two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus, saying, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for someone else?’
They came to Jesus and said to him, ‘John the Baptist sent us to you, saying, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for someone else?”’
At that very hour, he healed many people of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and gave sight to many who were blind.
Jesus answered them, ‘Go and tell John everything you have seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, those with leprosy are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, and the poor receive good news.
And blessed is anyone who does not stumble because of me.’
When John’s disciples had gone, he began to speak to the crowds about John: ‘What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothes? Look, those who wear splendid clothes and live in luxury are in kings’ palaces.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: “Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare the way before you.”’
I tell you that among those born of women there is no prophet greater than John the Baptist. Yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
All the people who heard, even the tax collectors, acknowledged that God was right, having received John’s baptism.
But the Pharisees and scribes rejected God’s will for themselves by refusing to be baptized by him.
‘To whom, then, shall I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?
They are like children sitting in the marketplace, calling out to their companions and saying, “We played music for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament for you, and you did not weep.”
For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, “He has a demon.”
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, “Look, a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!”
And wisdom is vindicated by all her children.
Then one of the Pharisees came and asked him to eat with him. He entered that Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
There was a sinful woman in that town. When she learned that he was reclining at the table in that Pharisee’s house, she brought a flask of perfume.
She stood behind him at his feet, weeping. She began wetting his feet with her tears and wiping them with the hair of her head. She kissed his feet and anointed them with perfume.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he thought to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who this woman touching him is and what sort of woman she is—that she is a sinner.”
Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said to him, “Speak, Teacher.” Jesus said to him:
“A certain creditor had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty denarii.
Since they had nothing with which to repay him, he forgave them both. Which of them, then, will love him more?”
Simon answered, “I suppose the one who was forgiven more.” Jesus said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
He turned toward the woman and said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house, and you gave me no water for my feet. But she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You did not kiss me, but from the time she came in, she has not stopped kissing my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfumed oil.
For this reason I tell you that her many sins are forgiven, because she has loved much. But whoever is forgiven little loves little.”
He said to the woman, “Your sins are forgiven.”
But those reclining at the table began saying to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
But Jesus said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
After these things, Jesus traveled through the towns and villages, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God. His twelve were with him,
and these women who had been healed of illnesses and evil spirits: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s household manager, and Susanna, and many other women who provided for them out of their own possessions.
When a large crowd had gathered and people were coming to him from every town, he spoke in parables:
“A sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell beside the road and was trampled, and the birds ate it.
Other seed fell on rock and sprouted immediately, but because it had no moisture, it withered.
Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up with it and choked it.
Other seed fell on good, fertile soil, grew, and produced a hundredfold crop.” As he said these things, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!”
His disciples asked him what this parable meant.

He said to them, “You have been given the knowledge of the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to the rest it is told in riddles, so that though they see, they may not see, and though they hear, they may not understand.
Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.
Those along the path are the ones who hear the word, but the enemy comes and takes the word from their hearts so that they will not believe and live.
Those on the rock are the ones who receive the word with joy when they hear it, but they have no root. Their faith lasts only for a time, and in a time of testing they fall away.
What fell among the thorns represents those who hear the word but are choked by worry, wealth, and the pleasures of the world, and bear no fruit.
What fell on good soil represents those who hear the word with a pure and good heart, hold on to it, and bear fruit with perseverance.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a container or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a lampstand so that everyone who comes in can see its light.
For nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and nothing is hidden that will not become known and come into the open.
Pay attention to how you listen. For whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have will have even what they think they have taken away from them.
His mother and his brothers came to him, but they could not speak with him because of the crowd.
They told him, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to see you.”
But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.”
One day Jesus got into a boat and sat down with his disciples. He said to them, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.”
As they sailed, Jesus fell asleep. A windstorm arose on the lake, and the boat was close to sinking.
They came and woke him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” He got up and rebuked the winds and the waves of the sea. They subsided, and there was a calm.
He said to them, “Where is your faith?” They were afraid and amazed, and said to one another, “Who is this, then, that he commands even the winds, the waves, and the sea, and they obey him?”
They sailed on and came to the region of the Gadarenes, which is on the other side, opposite Galilee.
When he stepped ashore, a man from the city met him who had had a demon for a long time. He wore no clothes and did not live in a house, but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, saying in a loud voice, “What do you have to do with us, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I beg you, do not torment me!”

For Jesus had been commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. It had held him captive for a long time. He would be bound with chains and kept under guard in shackles, but he would break his bonds and be driven by the demon into the wilderness.
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.
They begged him not to command them to go into the abyss.
There was a large herd of pigs grazing there on the mountain. They begged him to allow them to enter the pigs, and he allowed them.
The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs. The whole herd rushed toward the cliff, fell into the lake, and drowned.
When the herders saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the towns and villages.
People went out to see what had happened and came to Jesus. They found the man from whom the demons had come out clothed and in his right mind, sitting at Jesus’ feet, and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
The whole crowd of Gadarenes asked him to leave them, because great fear had seized them. So Jesus got into the boat and went back, leaving them.
The man from whom the demons had gone out begged him to let him stay with him. But Jesus sent him away and said to him,
“Return to your home and tell what God has done for you.” And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole town what Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, a large crowd welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
A man named Jairus, a synagogue leader, fell at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come into his house.
For he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was near death. As Jesus went with him, a large crowd pressed against him.
Now there was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all she owned on physicians, but no one had been able to heal her.
She came up behind him and touched the edge of his garment. Immediately her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When everyone denied it, Simon Peter and those with him said to him, “Master, the crowds are pressing against you and crowding you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
But he said, “Someone touched me, for I knew that power had gone out from me.”

When the woman saw that she had not escaped his notice, she came trembling, fell down, and bowed before him. In front of all the people, she told why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
Jesus said to her, “Take courage, my daughter. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader’s house and said to him, “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher.”
But Jesus heard and said to the girl’s father, “Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will live.”
Jesus came to the house and allowed no one to enter with him except Simon, James, John, and the girl’s father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and beating their breasts over her. But Jesus said, “Do not weep, for she has not died; she is sleeping.”
They laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
But he put everyone outside, took her by the hand, and called to her, saying, “Girl, get up.”
Her spirit returned, and she immediately got up. He ordered them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were astonished, but he warned them not to tell anyone what had happened.
Jesus called his twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, “Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bag, no bread, and no money. Do not have two tunics.
Whatever house you enter, stay there, and leave from there.
Wherever people do not welcome you, when you leave that town, shake even the dust off your feet as a testimony against them.”
The apostles went out and traveled through the villages and towns, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard about everything that was happening through him and was bewildered, because some people were saying that John had risen from the dead.
Others were saying that Elijah had appeared, and others that a prophet from among the prophets of old had risen.
Herod said, “I cut off John’s head. Who, then, is this man about whom I hear these things?” And he wanted to see him.
When the apostles returned, they told Jesus everything they had done. He took them away by themselves to a deserted place at Bethsaida.
But when the crowds learned about it, they followed him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those who needed healing.

As the day began to draw to a close, his disciples came to him and said, “Send the crowds away so that they can go to the surrounding villages and hamlets to find lodging and food for themselves, because we are in a deserted place.”
Jesus said to them, “You give them something to eat.” But they said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people.”
For there were about five thousand men. Jesus said to them, “Have them sit down in groups, fifty people in each group.”
The disciples did so and had them all sit down.
Jesus took those five loaves and two fish and looked up to heaven. He blessed them, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to set before the crowds.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered up twelve baskets of leftover pieces.
While he was praying alone, with his disciples beside him, he asked them, “Who do the crowds say I am?”
They answered him, “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and others say that one of the prophets of old has risen.”
He said to them, “But who do you say I am?” Simon answered, “The Messiah of God.”
But he sternly rebuked them and warned them not to tell anyone this.
He told them that the Son of Man would suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and that they would kill him, and on the third day he would rise.
He said before everyone, “Whoever wants to come after me must deny himself, take up his cross every day, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
For what benefit is it to a person to gain the whole world but lose himself or suffer loss?
Whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his Father’s glory with his holy angels.
Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.”
About eight days after these sayings, Jesus took Simon, James, and John with him and went up the mountain to pray.
While he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothes became white and gleaming.
And there were two men talking with him: Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glory and were speaking about his departure, which was to be accomplished in Jerusalem.
Simon and those with him were weighed down with sleep. With difficulty they woke up and saw his glory and the two men standing beside him.
As they began to leave him, Simon said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” He did not know what he was saying.
While he was saying these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them. They were afraid when they saw Moses and Elijah enter the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They kept silent and told no one in those days anything they had seen.
The next day, as they were coming down from the mountain, a large crowd met them.
A man from that crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg you, turn your attention to me. My son is my only child.
A spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, grinds his teeth, and foams at the mouth. It hardly leaves him, even after it has battered him.
I begged your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”
Jesus answered, “You unbelieving and twisted generation! How long must I be with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”
As he was bringing him near, the demon threw him down and convulsed him. Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
They were all amazed at the greatness of God. While everyone was marveling at everything Jesus was doing, he said to his disciples,
“Take these words to heart, for the Son of Man is going to be handed over into human hands.”
But they did not understand this saying, because it was hidden from them so that they would not understand it. They were afraid to ask him about this saying.
A thought arose among them about which of them was the greatest.
But Jesus knew the thought in their hearts. He took a child and stood him beside him,
and said to them, “Whoever welcomes a child like this in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. For whoever is least among you all will be great.”
John responded, “Our teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we stopped him because he did not follow you with us.”
Jesus said to them, “Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you.”
As the time for his being taken up drew near, he firmly resolved to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of him. They went and entered a Samaritan village to make preparations for him.
But they did not welcome him, because he was intent on going to Jerusalem.
When his disciples James and John saw this, they said to him, “Our Lord, do you want us to tell fire to come down from heaven and consume them, as Elijah did?”
He turned and rebuked them, saying, “You do not know what spirit you are of.”
“For the Son of Man did not come to destroy lives, but to save them.” And they went to another village.
As they were traveling along the road, someone said to him, “Lord, I will follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have shelters, but the Son of Man has nowhere to rest his head.”
He said to another, “Follow me.” But he said to him, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
Jesus said to him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. But you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
Another said to him, “I will follow you, Lord, but first let me go and say goodbye to my household, and then I will come.”
Jesus said to him, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
After this, Jesus chose seventy others from among his disciples and sent them ahead of him in pairs to every place and town where he was about to go.
He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. So ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.”
“Go! Look, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.”
“Do not take money pouches, traveling bags, or sandals, and do not greet anyone along the road.”
“Whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’”
“If a peaceful person is there, your peace will rest on him. But if not, it will return to you.”
“Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they have, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from house to house.”
“Whatever town you enter where they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.”
“Heal those in it who are sick, and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’”
“But whatever town you enter where they do not welcome you, go out into its street and say,”
“‘Even the dust from your town that clings to our feet, we shake off against you. Nevertheless, know this: the kingdom of God has come near to you.’”
“I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom on that day than for that town.”
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.”
“But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.”
“And you, Capernaum, who have been exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Sheol.”
Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.
The seventy whom he had sent returned with great joy and said to him, “Our Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name!”
He said to them, “I was watching Satan fall like lightning from heaven.”
Look, I give you authority to trample snakes and scorpions and all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice that the demons submit to you. Instead, rejoice that your names have been written in heaven.

At that very moment Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I thank you, my Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and discerning and revealed them to little children. Yes, my Father, for this was your good pleasure.”

He turned to his disciples and said to them, “Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.”
He turned to his disciples privately and said, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
For I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it.”
Then a scribe stood up to test him and said, “Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “What is written in the Law? How do you read it?”
He answered him, “Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
Jesus said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
But he, wanting to justify himself, said to him, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus said to him, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and robbers attacked him. They stripped him and beat him, and left him with barely any life remaining in him and went away.
A priest happened to be going down that road. He saw him and passed by.
Likewise, a Levite also came to that place, saw him, and passed by.
But a Samaritan who was traveling came to where he was. He saw him and had compassion on him.
He came near and bandaged his wounds, pouring wine and oil on them. He put him on his donkey, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The next morning he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. If you spend anything more, I will repay you when I return.’
Which of these three, then, seems to you to have been a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
He said, “The one who had compassion on him.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do the same yourself.”
As they were traveling along the road, he entered a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
She had a sister named Mary, who came and sat at our Lord’s feet and listened to his words.
But Martha was occupied with much serving. She came and said to him, “My Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me.”
Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about many things.”
“But only one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her.”
While he was praying in a certain place, when he had finished, one of his disciples said to him, “Our Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
Jesus said to them, “When you pray, say this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy. May your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us each day the bread we need.
And forgive us our sins, for we too forgive everyone who owes us. And do not bring us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’”
He said to them, “Which of you has a friend and goes to him at midnight and says to him, ‘My friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
because a friend has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
and his friend answers from inside and says to him, ‘Do not bother me. Look, the door is shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give you anything’?
I tell you, even if he will not give him anything because of their friendship, because of his shameless persistence he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
And I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Which father among you, if his son asks him for bread, will hand him a stone? And if he asks him for a fish, will he hand him a snake instead of a fish?
And if he asks him for an egg, will he hand him a scorpion?
And if you, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father give the Holy Spirit from heaven to those who ask him!”
While he was driving out a demon that was mute, when the demon came out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.
But some of them said, “This man drives out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
Others, testing him, were asking him for a sign from heaven.
But Jesus, who knew their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be ruined, and a household divided against itself will fall.”
“And if Satan is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his courtyard, his possessions are safe.
But if someone stronger than he comes and defeats him, he takes away all the armor in which he trusted and divides up his plunder.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

When an unclean spirit comes out of a person, it wanders through places where there is no water, seeking rest for itself. When it does not find any, it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came out.’
And when it comes, it finds it swept and put in order.
Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and live there. And that person's final condition becomes worse than the first.
While he was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that carried you, and the breasts that nursed you!”
But he said to her, “Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”
As the crowds were gathering, he began to say, “This evil generation seeks a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will also be a sign to this generation.

The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom. And look, someone greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah's preaching. And look, someone greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place or under a measuring basket, but on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see its light.
Your eye is the lamp of your body. So when your eye is sound, your whole body will also be full of light. But if it is bad, your body will also be dark.
So take care that the light in you is not darkness.
If your whole body is full of light, with no dark part in it, it will be entirely illuminated, just as a lamp gives you light with its flame.”
While he was speaking, a Pharisee asked him to eat with him. So he went in and reclined at the table.
When the Pharisee saw him, he was surprised that he had not first washed before his meal.
But Jesus said to him, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of plunder and wickedness.
You fools! Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
But give what you have as charity, and then everything will be clean for you.
But woe to you Pharisees! You give a tenth of mint, rue, and every vegetable, but neglect justice and the love of God. You ought to have practiced these without neglecting the others.
Woe to you Pharisees! You love the seats of honor in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You are like unmarked graves that people walk over without knowing it.”
One of the scribes answered him, “Teacher, when you say these things, you insult us too.”
But he said, “Woe to you scribes too! You load people with heavy burdens, but you yourselves do not touch those burdens with even one of your fingers.
Woe to you! You build the tombs of the prophets whom your ancestors killed.
So you testify to and approve of your ancestors' deeds, because they killed them, and you build their tombs.
For this reason the wisdom of God also said, ‘Look, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will persecute and kill.’
so that this generation may be held accountable for the blood of all the prophets shed since the world was created,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the temple and the altar. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be held accountable for it.
Woe to you, scribes! You have taken away the keys of knowledge. You did not enter yourselves, and you prevented those who were entering.
When he said these things to them, the scribes and Pharisees began to resent it, becoming angry and criticizing his words,
and plotting against him in many ways, trying to catch something from his mouth so that they could accuse him.

When tens of thousands had gathered in large crowds, so that they were trampling one another, Jesus began to say to his disciples, “First, guard yourselves against the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
There is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not become known.
For everything you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered into ears in private rooms will be proclaimed on the rooftops.
But I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and afterward can do nothing more.
But I will show you whom you should fear: the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
But even the hairs on your heads are all counted. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
But whoever denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you into the synagogues, before rulers and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
For the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.”
Someone from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
But Jesus said to him, “Man, who appointed me as a judge or divider over you?”
He said to his disciples, “Beware of every kind of greed, because life does not consist in an abundance of possessions.”
He told them a parable: “A certain rich man's land produced abundant crops.
He thought to himself, “What should I do? I have nowhere to store my crops.”
And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my storehouses and rebuild them larger, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
And I will say to my soul, “My soul, you have many good things stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.”’
But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your soul will be demanded from you. And whose will these things be that you have prepared?’
That is how it is with someone who stores up treasures for himself but is not rich toward God.”
He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, and they have neither storerooms nor barns, yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than birds!
Which of you can add one cubit to his height by worrying?
If you cannot do even such a small thing, why worry about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass that is in the field today and is thrown into the oven tomorrow, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith!
Do not seek what you will eat or what you will drink, and do not let your minds be preoccupied with these things.
For the nations of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows that you too need them.
Instead, seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be given to you as well.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to charity. Make yourselves money bags that do not wear out, and a treasure in heaven that does not run out, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.
Keep your belts fastened around your waists and your lamps burning.
Be like people waiting for their master to return from a banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him immediately.
Blessed are those servants whom their master finds awake when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt around his waist, have them recline at the table, and come and serve them.
If he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them like this, blessed are those servants!
But know this: if the owner of the house had known during which watch the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
You too, therefore, must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”
Simon Peter said to him, “Our Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone as well?”
Jesus said to him, “Who, then, is the faithful and wise household manager whom his master will put in charge of his servants, to give them their food allowance at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing this when he comes.
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’ and begins beating his master's male and female servants, and begins eating, drinking, and getting drunk,
that servant's master will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him in two and assign him a place with the unfaithful.
The servant who knows his master's will but does not prepare himself according to his will shall receive many blows.

But the one who does not know and does something deserving of blows will receive few blows. For everyone who has been given much will have much required of him, and from the one entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.
I came to cast fire on the earth, and I wish it were already burning!
I have a baptism to undergo, and I am deeply distressed until it is completed.
Do you think I came to bring peace on the earth? I tell you, no, but division.
For from now on, five people in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.

For father will be divided against son, and son against his father; mother against her daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
He said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say, ‘Rain is coming,’ and so it happens.
And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.
Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you do not interpret this present time?
And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For when you are going with your accuser to the magistrate, make an effort to settle with him while you are still on the way, so that he does not take you before the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
And I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last penny.”
At that time some people came and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Jesus answered them, “Do you think these Galileans were greater sinners than all the other Galileans because this happened to them?
No! But I tell you, unless you repent, you too will all perish in the same way.
Or those eighteen people on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think they were greater sinners than all the other people living in Jerusalem?
No! But I tell you, unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.”
He told this parable: “A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it but found none.
He said to the gardener, “Look, for three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and have found none. Cut it down. Why should it take up the ground for nothing?”
The gardener said to him, ‘Sir, leave it this year too, while I cultivate it and fertilize it.
And if it bears fruit—but if not, you can cut it down next year.’”
While Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath,
there was a woman there who had had a spirit of illness for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
Jesus saw her, called her over, and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your illness.”
He laid his hand on her, and immediately she straightened up and praised God.

But the synagogue leader, angry because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded by saying to the crowds, “There are six days on which work should be done. Come on those days and be healed, not on the Sabbath day.”
Jesus answered him, “Hypocrite! Does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from the feeding trough on the Sabbath and lead it away to give it water?
But this woman is a daughter of Abraham, whom the devil has bound for eighteen years now. Should she not have been freed from this bond on the Sabbath day?”
As he said these things, all those who opposed him were put to shame, and all the people rejoiced at all the wonderful things being done through him.
Then Jesus said, “What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?”
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.
Again Jesus said, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?”
“It is like yeast that a woman took and hid in three seahs of flour until the whole batch was leavened.”
He traveled through villages and towns, teaching as he made his way to Jerusalem.
Someone asked him, “Are those who are saved few?”
Jesus said to them, “Strive to enter through the narrow door, for I tell you that many will seek to enter and will not be able.

Once the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside and knock at the door. You will begin to say, ‘Our Lord, our Lord, open the door for us!’ But he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know you or where you come from.’
Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
But he will say to you, ‘I do not know you or where you come from. Get away from me, you who practice deceit!’
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, while you yourselves are thrown outside.
People will come from the east and the west, from the south and the north, and recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
Look, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”
That very day, some Pharisees approached and said to him, “Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill you.”
Jesus said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look, I am casting out demons and performing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will be brought to completion.’
Nevertheless, I must go about today and tomorrow, and leave on the following day, because a prophet cannot perish outside Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
Look, your house is left to you desolate. For I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
When he went into the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees to eat a meal on the Sabbath, they were watching him closely.
There before him was a man whose body was swollen with fluid.
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees, asking, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
But they remained silent. He took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
Then he said to them, “Which of you, if his son or his ox falls into a well on the Sabbath day, will not immediately pull him up and out?”
They could give him no answer to this.
He told a parable to those invited there, because he saw them choosing the places of honor at the tables.
When someone invites you to a banquet, do not go and take the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited there.
Then the one who invited both you and him may come and say to you, “Give this man your place,” and you will be ashamed as you get up and take the lowest place.

Instead, when you are invited, go and take the lowest place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, “My friend, move up higher and take your place.” Then you will be honored before everyone dining with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself will be exalted.

He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you give a lunch or dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, or your rich neighbors, in case they invite you in return and that becomes your repayment.
Instead, when you give a reception, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind.
Then you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
When one of those dining with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is the person who will eat bread in the kingdom of God!”
Jesus said to him, “A man gave a great dinner and invited many people.
At dinnertime he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, “Look, everything is ready for you. Come!”
But they all alike began to excuse themselves. The first said to him, “I have bought an estate, and I must go out and see it. Please excuse me.”
Another said, “I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.”
Another said, “I have married a wife, and for that reason I cannot come.”

The servant came and told his master these things. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant, “Go out quickly into the streets and open squares of the city, and bring in here the poor, the afflicted, the lame, and the blind.”
The servant said, “Master, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.”
The master said to his servant, “Go out to the roads and among the hedges, and compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled.
For I tell you, not one of those people who were invited will taste my dinner.”
As large crowds were traveling with him, he turned and said to them:
“Anyone who comes to me and does not hate his father and mother, his brothers and sisters, his wife and children, and even his own life, cannot be my disciple.
Anyone who does not carry his cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate its cost to see whether he has enough to finish it?
Otherwise, after he has laid the foundation and cannot finish, everyone who sees it will mock him,
saying, “This man began to build and could not finish.”
Or what king goes to war to fight another king without first considering whether he can, with ten thousand men, meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
But if not, while the other is still far away from him, he sends messengers and asks for peace.
So none of you who does not give up all his possessions can be my disciple.
Salt is good, but if even salt loses its flavor, what can make it salty again?
It is fit neither for the soil nor for manure. They throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
Tax collectors and sinners were coming near him to listen to him.
