The scribes and Pharisees were grumbling and saying, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
Jesus told them this parable:
“Which of you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go looking for the lost one until he finds it?
When he finds it, he rejoices and lifts it onto his shoulders.
He comes home and calls his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.’
I tell you, in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need repentance.
Or what woman, if she has ten silver coins and loses one of them, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully for it until she finds it?
When she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my coin that was lost.’
I tell you, in the same way there will be joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”
Jesus also said to them, “A certain man had two sons.
His younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me the share of your estate that belongs to me.’ So he divided his property between them.
A few days later, the younger son gathered together everything that had come to him and went to a distant country. There he squandered his possessions by living recklessly.
When he had used up everything he had, a severe famine struck that country, and he began to be in need.
He went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him to his farm to tend pigs.
He longed to fill his stomach with the carob pods the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
When he came to his senses, he said, ‘How many hired workers in my father’s house have more than enough bread, while I am here dying of hunger!
I will get up and go to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.’
So he got up and went to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and had compassion on him. He ran, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him.
His son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am not worthy to be called your son.’
But his father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and dress him in it. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened ox and slaughter it. Let us eat and celebrate.
For this son of mine was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found. And they began to celebrate.
Now his older son was out in the country. As he came and approached the house, he heard the sound of many people making music.
He called one of the servants and asked him, “What is this?”
He told him, “Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened ox because he has received him back in good health.”
He became angry and would not go in. His father came out and pleaded with him.

But he said to his father, “Look, all these years I have worked for you like a slave, and I have never disobeyed your command. Yet you have never given me a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came back after squandering your property with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened ox for him.”
His father said to him, “My son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.”
But it was right for us to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life, and was lost and has been found.
He told his disciples a parable: “There was a rich man who had a household manager. An accusation was brought to him that this manager was squandering his property.
His master called him and said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give me an account of your management, for you can no longer be my household manager.’
The household manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do? My master is taking my position as manager away from me. I cannot dig, and I am ashamed to beg.’
I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from my position as manager, they will welcome me into their homes.
He called his master’s debtors one by one and said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
He said to him, “A hundred measures of oil.” He said to him, “Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty measures.”
He said to another, ‘And you, what do you owe my master?’ He told him, ‘A hundred kors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, sit down, and write eighty kors.’
Our Lord praised the dishonest household manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the children of this world are shrewder in dealing with their own generation than the children of light.
And I also tell you: make friends for yourselves with this unrighteous wealth, so that when it runs out, they may welcome you into their eternal dwellings.
Whoever is faithful with a little is also faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with a little is also dishonest with much.
So if you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust true riches to you?
And if you have not proved faithful with what is not yours, who will give you what is your own?
No servant can serve two masters. For either he will hate one and love the other, or he will honor one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
When the Pharisees heard all these things, they mocked him, because they loved money.
But Jesus said to them, “You are the ones who make yourselves out to be righteous before people, but God knows your hearts. For what is highly esteemed among people is detestable before God.
The Law and the Prophets lasted until John. Since then, the kingdom of God has been proclaimed as good news, and everyone presses to enter it.
But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one letter of the Law to pass away.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and everyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
There was a rich man who wore fine linen and purple and enjoyed himself lavishly every day.
There was a poor man named Lazarus who lay at that rich man's gate, covered with sores.
He longed to fill his stomach with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table. Even the dogs would come and lick his sores.
The poor man died, and the angels carried him to Abraham's embrace. The rich man also died and was buried.
While he was being tormented in Sheol, he looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus in his embrace.
He called out loudly, saying, "My father Abraham, have mercy on me! Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and moisten my tongue, for I am being tormented in this flame."
Abraham said to him, "My son, remember that you received your good things during your life, while Lazarus received his bad things. Now, look, he is at rest here, while you are being tormented.
Besides all this, a great chasm has been set between us and you, so that those who want to cross from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross from there to us."
He said to him, "Then I beg you, my father, to send him to my father's house.
For I have five brothers. Let him go and warn them, so that they too do not come to this place of torment."
Abraham said to him, "They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them."
But he said to him, "No, my father Abraham! But if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent."
Abraham said to him, "If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not believe someone even if he rises from the dead."
Jesus said to his disciples, "It is impossible for things that cause people to stumble not to come, but woe to the person through whom they come!
It would be better for him to have a millstone turned by a donkey hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.
Even if he wrongs you seven times in a day and returns to you seven times in a day, saying, 'I repent,' forgive him."
The apostles said to our Lord, "Increase our faith."
He said to them, "If you had faith like a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Which of you, having a servant who plows or tends sheep, would say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Come in at once and sit down to eat'?
Instead, he says to him, “Prepare something for my supper, fasten your belt, and serve me while I eat and drink. Afterward, you too may eat and drink.”
Does he thank that servant for doing what he was commanded? I do not think so.
So you too, when you have done everything you were commanded, say, 'We are unworthy servants. We have done what we were obliged to do.'"
As Jesus was going to Jerusalem, he passed between Samaria and Galilee.
As he was about to enter a village, ten men with leprosy met him. They stood at a distance
and raised their voices, saying, "Jesus, our Master, have mercy on us!"
When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
But one of them, when he saw that he had been cleansed, turned back, praising God in a loud voice.
He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet, thanking him. This man was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered, “Were not ten cleansed? Where are the nine?
Why did they refrain from coming to give glory to God, except this man from a foreign people?”
He said to him, “Get up and go. Your faith has saved you.”
When some of the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come, he answered them, “The kingdom of God does not come with signs that can be watched for.
Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is!’ or ‘Look, there it is!’ For look, the kingdom of God is within you.”
He said to his disciples, “Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
If they say to you, ‘Look, here he is!’ or ‘Look, there he is!’ do not go.
For just as lightning flashes from the sky and lights up everything beneath the sky, so will the Son of Man be on his day.
But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
Just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
They were eating and drinking, marrying wives and being given to husbands, until the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed everyone.
Likewise, as it was in the days of Lot: they were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
But on the day Lot left Sodom, the Lord rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed them all.
So it will be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, anyone on the roof whose belongings are in the house must not go down to get them. And anyone in the field must not turn back.
Remember Lot’s wife.
Whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life will save it.
I tell you, on that night two will be in one bed. One will be taken and the other left.
Two women will be grinding together. One will be taken and the other left.
Two will be in the field. One will be taken and the other left.”
They answered him, “Where, our Lord?” He said to them, “Where the body is, there the eagles will gather.”
He also told them a parable about praying at all times and not becoming discouraged.
“There was a judge in a certain city who neither feared God nor had any regard for people.
There was a widow in that city who kept coming to him and saying, ‘Give me justice against my opponent.’
For a long time he was unwilling. But afterward he said to himself, ‘Even though I do not fear God or have any regard for people,
Yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will grant her justice, so that she does not keep coming and wearing me out.
And our Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge said.
Will not God all the more bring justice for his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night, while he is patient with them?
I tell you that he will bring them justice quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"
He also told this parable against people who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and despised everyone else:
"Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed these words: 'God, I thank you that I am not like other people—robbers, wrongdoers, and adulterers—or like this tax collector.
But I fast twice a week and give a tenth of everything I acquire.
But the tax collector stood at a distance and would not even lift his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his chest and said, 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner.'
I tell you that this man went down to his house justified rather than that Pharisee. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself will be exalted."
People were also bringing infants to him so that he would touch them. When his disciples saw them, they rebuked them.
But Jesus called them and said to them, “Let the children come to me, and do not stop them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to those who are like these children.”
"Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it."
One of the rulers asked him, "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one: God.
You know the commandments: Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Honor your father and your mother."
He said to him, "I have kept all these from my youth."
When Jesus heard this, he said to him, "You lack one thing. Go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."
But when he heard this, he became sad, for he was very rich.
When Jesus saw that he had become sad, he said, "How difficult it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
Those who heard said to him, "Then who can be saved?"
But Jesus said, "What is impossible for human beings is possible with God."
Simon Peter said to him, "Look, we have left everything and followed you."
Jesus said to him, "Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left houses or parents or brothers or a wife or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive many times as much in this time, and eternal life in the age to come."
Jesus took his twelve aside and said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written in the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
For he will be handed over to the Gentiles, and they will mock him and spit in his face.
They will flog him, insult him, and kill him, and on the third day he will rise.
But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was being said to them.
As he approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
He heard the sound of a crowd passing by and asked who it was.
They told him, “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.”
He cried out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Those walking ahead of Jesus rebuked him and told him to be quiet. But he cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and ordered them to bring him to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “My Lord, let me see.”
Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight! Your faith has made you well.”
Immediately he could see, and he followed him, praising God. All the people who saw it gave glory to God.
As Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through,
there was a man named Zacchaeus, who was rich and was a chief tax collector.
He wanted to see who Jesus was, but he could not because of the crowd, since Zacchaeus was short.
He ran ahead of Jesus and climbed a sycamore fig tree to see him, because he was going to pass that way.
When Jesus came to that place, he saw him and said to him, “Hurry and come down, Zacchaeus, for today I must stay at your house.”
He hurried down and welcomed him joyfully.
When they all saw this, they grumbled and said, “He has gone in to stay with a sinful man.”
But Zacchaeus stood and said to Jesus, “Look, my Lord, I give half my possessions to the poor, and whatever I have taken from anyone by fraud, I repay four times as much.”
Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and save what was lost.”
While they were listening to these things, he went on to tell a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was about to be revealed immediately.
He said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to receive royal authority for himself and then return.
He called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. He told them, ‘Do business with this until I return.’
But his fellow citizens hated him and sent messengers after him, saying, ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’
When he had received the kingdom and returned, he ordered those servants to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he could find out what each of them had gained by trading.
The first came and said, “My lord, your mina has earned ten minas.”
He said to him, “Well done, good servant! Because you have proved faithful with a little, you will have authority over ten cities.”
The second came and said, “My lord, your mina has made five minas.”
He said to this one too, “You too will have authority over five cities.”
Another came and said, “My lord, here is your mina, which I kept with me, wrapped in a cloth.
For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You take what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.”
He said to him, “I will judge you by your own words, wicked servant! You knew that I was a harsh man, taking what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow.
Why did you not put my money with a banker? Then, when I returned, I could have collected it with interest.”
He said to those standing before him, “Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.”
They said to him, “Our lord, he has ten minas!”
He said to them, “I tell you that everyone who has will be given more, but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
But bring here those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, and kill them in front of me.”
After Jesus had said these things, he went on ahead toward Jerusalem.
As he approached Bethphage and Bethany, beside the mountain called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples
and said to them, “Go to the village opposite us. As you enter it, you will find a colt tied up that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it.
If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him, ‘Our Lord needs it.’”
Those who were sent went and found it just as he had told them.
As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying that colt?”
They said to them, “Our Lord needs it.”
They brought it to Jesus, threw their cloaks over the colt, and helped Jesus mount it.
As he went along, they spread their cloaks on the road.
As he approached the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples began rejoicing and praising God in a loud voice for all the mighty deeds they had seen.
They were saying, “Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
Some of the Pharisees among the crowds said to him, “Rabbi, rebuke your disciples!”
He said to them, “I tell you, if these are silent, the stones will cry out!”
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it.
He said, “If only you knew, even on this day of yours, what would bring you peace! But now these things are hidden from your eyes.
Days will come upon you when your enemies will surround you and press you hard from every side.
They will level you to the ground, along with your children within you. They will not leave one stone upon another in you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.”
When he entered the temple, he began driving out those who were buying and selling in it.
He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers.”
He was teaching every day in the temple, but the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people were seeking to kill him.
They could not find a way to act against him, because all the people hung on his words as they listened to him.
One day, as he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, confronted him.
They said to him, “Tell us by what authority you do these things, and who gave you this authority.”
Jesus answered them, “I too will ask you a question. Tell me:
Was John’s baptism from heaven or from human beings?”
They discussed it among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ all the people will stone us, because they are convinced that John is a prophet.”
So they said to him, “We do not know where it was from.”
Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
He began telling the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, leased it to tenant farmers, and went away for a long time.
At the proper time he sent his servant to the tenant farmers so that they would give him some of the vineyard’s fruit. But the tenant farmers beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
He sent another servant, but they beat and insulted that one too and sent him away empty-handed.
He then sent a third, but they wounded that one too and threw him out.
The owner of the vineyard said, ‘What should I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps when they see him, they will show respect.’
But when the tenant farmers saw him, they discussed it among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
They threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.” When they heard this, they said, “May this never happen!”
But he looked at them and said, “Then what does this mean that is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone’?
Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, and anyone it falls on, it will crush.
The chief priests and scribes wanted to lay hands on him that very hour, but they were afraid of the people, for they knew that he had told this parable against them.
They sent spies to him who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch him in something he said and hand him over to the judge and to the governor’s authority.
They questioned him, saying, “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly and show no partiality, but teach the way of God truthfully.
Is it lawful for us to pay the poll tax to Caesar or not?”
But he recognized their cunning and said, “Why are you testing me?
Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it bear?” They said, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus said to them, “Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and God what belongs to God.”
They could not catch him in anything he said before the people. They were amazed at his answer and fell silent.
Some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came forward and questioned him,
saying to him, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies, leaving a wife but no children, the man must marry his brother’s wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died without children.
The second married her, and he too died without children.
Then the third married her, and likewise all seven married her and died, leaving no children.
Finally, the woman also died.
In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven married her.”
Jesus said to them, “The people of this age marry wives, and women marry husbands.
But those who are considered worthy of that age and of the resurrection from the dead neither marry wives, nor do women marry husbands.
For they can no longer die, because they are like angels. They are children of God, because they have become children of the resurrection.
Even Moses showed that the dead rise, for in the passage about the bush he said, ‘The Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for they are all alive to him.”
Some of the scribes responded, saying to him, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”
And they no longer dared to question him about anything.
He said to them, “How do the scribes say that the Messiah is David’s son?
David himself said in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand
until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
If David, then, calls him ‘my Lord,’ how is he his son?
While all the people were listening, he said to his disciples:
Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes and love greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at dinners.
“They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers as a pretense. They will receive a harsher judgment.”
Jesus looked at the rich people who were putting their offerings into the treasury.
He also saw a poor widow who put in two small coins.
He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than everyone else.
For all these people put offerings into God’s treasury out of their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had.”
While some people were speaking about the temple, saying that it was adorned with beautiful stones and offerings, Jesus said to them:
“As for these things you see, days will come when not one stone will be left upon another without being torn down.”
They asked him, “Teacher, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that these things are about to happen?”
He said to them, “Take care that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name and say, ‘I am the Messiah,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ But do not follow them.”
“When you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be afraid. These things must happen first, but the end has not yet come.”
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
“There will be great earthquakes in various places, and famines and plagues. There will be terrors and alarming events, and great signs will appear from heaven. There will also be great storms.
But before all these things, they will lay hands on you and persecute you. They will hand you over to synagogues and prisons, and bring you before kings and governors because of my name.
But this will be an opportunity for you to testify.
So make up your minds not to rehearse your defense.
For I will give you words and wisdom that none of your enemies will be able to withstand.
Your parents, brothers, relatives, and friends will betray you, and they will put some of you to death.
Everyone will hate you because of my name.
Not a hair of your heads will be lost.
But by your endurance you will gain your lives.
“When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its destruction is near.
Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, those inside the city must flee, and those in the villages must not enter it.
For these are days of retribution, so that everything written may be fulfilled.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing babies in those days! For there will be great distress in the land and wrath against this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive everywhere. Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
“There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and on earth distress among the nations, and helplessness from bewilderment at the roaring of the sea,
and trembling that takes people’s lives from fear of what is about to come upon the earth. And the powers of heaven will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and great glory.
But when these things begin to happen, take courage and lift up your heads, because your deliverance is drawing near.
He told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.”
When they sprout, you immediately know from them that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But watch yourselves, so that your hearts are never weighed down by excess, drunkenness, and worldly worries, and that day does not come upon you suddenly.
For it will spring like a trap on all those who live on the face of the whole earth.
So stay alert at all times and pray that you may be found worthy to escape these things that are going to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
During the day he would teach in the temple, and at night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain called the Mount of Olives.
All the people would come to him early in the temple to hear his word.
Now the Festival of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was near.
The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to kill him, for they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered Judas, who was called Iscariot and was one of the Twelve.
He went and spoke with the chief priests, the scribes, and the commanders of the temple guard about how he could hand him over to them.
They were glad and agreed to give him money.
He promised them and began looking for an opportunity to hand him over to them without a crowd present.
Then the day of Unleavened Bread arrived, on which it was customary to slaughter the Passover sacrifice.
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying to them, “Go and prepare the Passover meal for us to eat.”
They said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare it?”
He said to them, “Look, when you enter the city, a man carrying a waterskin will meet you. Follow him.
Wherever he goes in, say to the owner of the house, ‘Our teacher says: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover meal with my disciples?’
He will show you a large upstairs room that is furnished. Make preparations there.”
They went and found everything just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
When the time came, Jesus came and reclined at the table, and the twelve apostles were with him.
He said to them, “I have deeply longed to eat this Passover meal with you before I suffer.
For I tell you that from now on I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
He took a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Take this and share it among yourselves.
For I tell you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”
He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Keep doing this in remembrance of me.”
Likewise, after they had eaten supper, he said over the cup, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.”
“But look, the hand of the one who betrays me is on the table.”
“The Son of Man goes as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
They began to ask one another which of them it could be who was going to do this.
There was also a dispute among them about which of them was the greatest.
But Jesus said to them, “The kings of the nations are their masters, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors.”
“But you must not be like that. Instead, let the greatest among you become like the youngest, and the leader like one who serves.”
“For who is greater: the one reclining at the table or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.”
“But you are the ones who have stayed with me through my trials.”
“And I promise you a kingdom, just as my Father promised me,”
“so that you may eat and drink at the table of my kingdom, and sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.”
Jesus said to Simon, “Simon, look, Satan has asked to sift you like wheat.”
But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail. And you, in time, turn back and strengthen your brothers.
But Simon said to him, “My Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death.”
Jesus said to him, “I tell you, Simon, the rooster will not crow today until you have said three times that you do not know me.”
He said to them, “When I sent you out without money bags, traveling bags, or sandals, did you lack anything?” They said to him, “Nothing.”
He said to them, “From now on, whoever has a money bag should take it, and likewise a traveling bag. And whoever has no sword should sell his garment and buy himself a sword.”
“For I tell you that this too, which is written, must be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted among wrongdoers.’ For everything concerning me has been fulfilled.”
They said to him, “Our Lord, look, here are two swords.” He said to them, “They are enough.”
He went out and went to the Mount of Olives, as was his custom, and his disciples also followed him.
When he reached the place, he said to them, “Pray that you do not enter into temptation.”
He withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, knelt down, and prayed,
saying, “Father, if you are willing, let this cup pass from me. Yet let not my will, but yours, be done.”
An angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him.
In anguish, he prayed earnestly. His sweat became like drops of blood and fell to the ground.
He rose from prayer and came to his disciples, and found them sleeping from sorrow.
He said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray that you do not enter into temptation.”

While he was still speaking, a crowd appeared. The man called Judas, one of the Twelve, was coming ahead of them. He approached Jesus and kissed him, for he had given them this sign: “The one I kiss is the man.”
Jesus said to him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
When those with him saw what was happening, they said to him, “Our Lord, shall we strike them with swords?”
One of them struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus answered, “Enough! No more of this!” He touched the ear of the man who had been struck and healed it.

Jesus said to those who had come against him—the chief priests, the elders, and the commanders of the temple guard—“Have you come out against me with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a robber?”
I was with you in the temple every day, and you did not lay hands on me. But this is your hour and the power of darkness.
They arrested him and brought him to the high priest’s house. Simon was following him at a distance.
They lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat around it. Simon himself was also sitting among them.
A young woman saw him sitting by the fire. She looked closely at him and said, “This man was with him too.”
But he denied it, saying, “Woman, I do not know him.”
A little later, someone else saw him and said to him, “You are one of them too.” But Peter said, “I am not.”
An hour later, another man insisted, saying, “This man certainly was with him too, for he is also a Galilean.”
Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are talking about.” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
Jesus turned and looked at Peter. Then Simon remembered what our Lord had said to him: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
Simon went outside and wept bitterly.
The men holding Jesus were mocking him and covering his face.
They struck him in the face and said, “Prophesy! Who hit you?”
They also said many other insulting things against him.
When day dawned, the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes gathered and brought him up to their council chamber.
They said to him, “If you are the Messiah, tell us.” He said to them, “If I tell you, you will not believe me.”
“And if I question you, you will not answer me or let me go.”
“From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
Then they all said, “Are you, then, the Son of God?” Jesus said to them, “You yourselves say that I am.”
They said, “Why do we need any more witnesses? We have heard it ourselves from his own mouth.”
Their whole assembly rose and brought him to Pilate.
They began accusing him, saying, “We found this man leading our people astray and forbidding us to pay the poll tax to Caesar. He says of himself that he is the Messiah, a king.”
Pilate questioned him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him, “You have said it.”
Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowd, “I find no grounds for a charge against this man.”
But they kept shouting, saying, “He has stirred up our people by teaching throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee and reaching as far as here.”
When Pilate heard Galilee mentioned, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
When he learned that he was under Herod’s authority, he sent him to Herod, because Herod was in Jerusalem during those days.
When Herod saw Jesus, he was very glad. He had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him, and he hoped to see him perform some miraculous sign.
He questioned him at length, but Jesus gave him no answer.
The chief priests and the scribes stood there, vehemently accusing him.
Herod and his soldiers treated him with contempt. Mocking him, Herod dressed him in scarlet clothing and sent him to Pilate.
That day Pilate and Herod became friends with each other, for previously there had been hostility between them.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

and said to them, “You brought this man to me as someone who was leading your people astray. Look, I have examined him in your presence, and I have found no grounds for a charge against this man in any of the accusations you bring against him.
Nor has Herod, for I sent him to him. Look, he has done nothing deserving death.
So I will punish him and release him.”
For there was a custom that he should release one prisoner for them at the festival.
But the whole crowd shouted, saying, “Take this man away and release Barabbas for us!”
He was the one who had been put in prison for an uprising that had taken place in the city, and for murder.
Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus.
But they kept shouting, “Crucify him! Crucify him!”
For the third time he said to them, “Why? What evil has this man done? I have found no grounds for a charge against him deserving death. So I will punish him and release him.”
But they kept pressing him with loud shouts, demanding that he be crucified. Their shouting and that of the chief priests grew stronger.
Pilate ordered that their demand be granted.
He released for them the man who had been put in prison for an uprising and murder, the one they had asked for. But he handed Jesus over to their will.
As they were leading him away, they seized Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the countryside, and laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
A large crowd of people followed him, along with women who were beating their breasts and mourning for him.
Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.”
For look, days are coming when they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that have not given birth, and the breasts that have not nursed.’
Then you will begin to say to the mountains, “Fall on us,” and to the hills, “Cover us.”
For if they do these things to green wood, what will happen to dry wood?
Two others, criminals, were also going with him to be put to death.
When they came to a place called the Skull, they crucified him there, along with the criminals, one on his right and one on his left.
But Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided his clothes and cast lots for them.
The people stood watching. The rulers also sneered at him, saying, “He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Messiah, God’s chosen one.”
The soldiers also mocked him, coming up to him and offering him vinegar.
They said to him, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.”
There was also an inscription written above him in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “This is the King of the Jews.”
One of the criminals who were crucified with him insulted him, saying, “If you are the Messiah, save yourself, and save us too.”
But his companion rebuked him and said to him, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
And we are being punished justly, for we have received what we deserve for what we did. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
And he said to Jesus, “Remember me, my Lord, when you come in your kingdom.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
It was about noon, and darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon.
The sun grew dark, and the curtain at the entrance of the temple was torn down the middle.
Jesus cried out in a loud voice and said, “My Father, into your hands I place my spirit.” After saying this, he died.
When the centurion saw what had happened, he praised God and said, “Truly, this man was righteous.”
All the crowds who had gathered for this spectacle, when they saw what had happened, went back beating their chests.
All those who knew Jesus, and the women who had come with him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things.
There was a man named Joseph, a council member from Arimathea, a town in Judea. He was a good and righteous man.
He had not agreed with their decision or their action, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
He took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid it in a tomb cut out of rock, in which no one had yet been laid.
It was Friday, and the Sabbath was about to begin.
The women who had come with him from Galilee came near and saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
They returned and prepared aromatic spices and perfumes. On the Sabbath they rested, as commanded.
On the first day of the week, early in the morning while it was still dark, they came to the tomb, bringing the aromatic spices they had prepared. Other women were with them.
They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
They went in but did not find the body of Jesus.
While they were bewildered about this, suddenly two men stood above them, and their clothing shone like lightning.
The women were afraid and bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, “Why are you looking for the living one among the dead?
He is not here; he has risen. Remember what he told you while he was in Galilee,
when he said that the Son of Man was to be handed over to sinful men, be crucified, and rise on the third day.”
Then they remembered his words.
They returned from the tomb and told all these things to the eleven and to the rest.
They were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles.
But these words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe the women.
But Simon got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down to look and saw the linen cloths lying there alone. Then he went away, wondering to himself about what had happened.
That same day, two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
While they were talking and discussing with each other, Jesus himself came, caught up with them, and walked with them.
But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
He said to them, “What are these things you are discussing with each other as you walk along, looking so sad?”
One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only stranger from Jerusalem who does not know what happened there in these days?”
He said to them, “What things?” They said to him, “About Jesus of Nazareth, a man who was a prophet, powerful in word and deed before God and all the people.
The chief priests and elders handed him over to be sentenced to death and crucified him.
But we had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. And now it has been three days since all these things happened.
Moreover, some women from our group amazed us. They had gone to the tomb early,
and when they did not find his body, they came and told us that they had seen angels there who said that he was alive.
Some of our men also went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.”
Then Jesus said to them, “You who lack understanding and are slow of heart to believe everything the prophets have spoken!
Wasn't the Messiah destined to endure these things and enter his glory?
And beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them what concerned himself in all the Scriptures.
They approached the village they were going to, and he made it seem to them that he was going on to a distant place.
They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, because the day is now drawing toward darkness.” And he went in to stay with them.
When he reclined at the table with them, he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
Immediately their eyes were opened, and they recognized him. Then he was taken away from them.
They said to one another, “Wasn't our heart heavy within us while he spoke with us on the road and explained the Scriptures to us?”
They got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem. They found the eleven gathered together, along with those who were with them.
They were saying, “Our Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon.”
They too recounted what had happened on the road and how he had made himself known to them when he broke the bread.
While they were speaking about these things, Jesus stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you. It is I. Do not be afraid.”
They were startled and frightened, for they thought they were seeing a spirit.
Jesus said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
Look at my hands and my feet: it is I myself. Touch me and know that a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”
After saying these things, he showed them his hands and his feet.
While they still did not believe because of their joy and were amazed, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave him a piece of roasted fish and some honeycomb.
He took it and ate it before their eyes.
He said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was with you: everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled.”
Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
He said to them, “This is what is written, and this is how it was necessary for the Messiah to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and for repentance for the forgiveness of sins to be proclaimed in his name among all nations. The beginning will be from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
And I will send upon you what my Father promised. But you must remain in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”
He led them out as far as Bethany, raised his hands, and blessed them.
While he was blessing them, he parted from them and went up to heaven.
They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
They were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
